A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Astute RAG, with matching algorithms and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Claude and Gemini experiments on four question-answering datasets, RGB robustness results, and quantitative and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Mistral evaluations, ASQA results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3 and v2 Section 4 retain the same adaptive passage generation, iterative source-aware consolidation, and answer finalization. Algorithm 1 and the three method prompts in Appendix A are substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds long-form question answering on ASQA (Section 5.2, Figure 5), extending beyond v1's short-form evaluation. NQ, TriviaQA, BioASQ, PopQA, and the negative-passage RGB scenario remain.

E2.justification: The original main-table comparators remain. Appendices C–E add evaluated Answer Refinement, retrieved-only Context Filtering, generated-and-retrieved Context Filtering, and CompAct baselines (Tables 4–7), substantially expanding comparisons with alternative correction and context-processing strategies.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral-Large and Mistral-Nemo model configurations, LLM judging of intermediate outputs, source-removal controls, passage-order experiments, and a maximum-generated-passages sweep. The retained short-form benchmark still contains 1,042 questions with ten passages each, and default Astute RAG settings remain one generated passage maximum and one consolidation iteration.

E4.justification: New analyses examine retrieval precision versus conflict rate, source-awareness, adaptive passage counts, intermediate-step correctness, token costs, filtering versus consolidation, and passage-order robustness. Earlier conflict-subset and qualitative analyses remain. Claude's iteration experiment is redisplayed, while the Gemini iteration analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added intermediate-step confidence-assignment evaluation does not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds ASQA results, Mistral overall accuracies of 59.9 and 51.3, and numerous ablation and comparator results. Retained Claude/Gemini default scores match apart from rounding. Figure 7 swaps the InstructRAG/Self-Route curve labels relative to v1 Figure 4a, aligning their aggregate ordering with the main table. Gemini's two- and three-iteration result rows disappear.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, source indicators, and generation/consolidation equations remain equivalent. Retrieval precision's displayed fraction becomes an equivalent verbal definition. No substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit introductory claim that retrieval precision is tightly correlated with knowledge-conflict rate, sharpening the empirical contribution beyond v1's broader diagnosis of retrieval failures and conflict prevalence. The central method and worst-case robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for reduced conflicts at zero retrieval precision, benefits of source information and consolidation over filtering/refinement, and CompAct's failures. It interprets results as supporting smaller-model applicability and reduced ordering sensitivity. The longer-output limitation becomes a longer-input limitation, while earlier Gemini iteration interpretations and context-type/multimodal future directions are removed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an intermediate-step judging prompt, added model versions and sizes, and a more specific RGB subset description. Existing method prompts and retrieval instructions remain. v1's explicit USC sampling temperature of 0.7 is omitted; this establishes a disclosure loss, not an actual temperature change.

R1.justification: v2 more explicitly acknowledges prior observations and adds references for practical knowledge conflicts, ASQA, CompAct, and passage ordering. Appendix E distinguishes consolidation from context compression. Several survey and future-work references disappear, while the broader training-free, black-box, post-retrieval positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and pitfall discussion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, problem formulation merges into the method overview, experimental discussion is reorganized, limitations receive a separate heading, and appendices expand from A–B to A–F.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, combines the original main tables, separates v1 Figure 4 into individual plots, and adds multiple figures and tables. Iteration and API-call results are redisplayed graphically, legends are revised, and several displays—including the retained qualitative examples—move after the references.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method. ASQA addresses v1's deferred long-form evaluation, while component ablations and filtering/refinement/compression comparisons test whether consolidation contributes beyond simpler alternatives. Smaller-model, ordering, and cost analyses further strengthen applicability evidence. Some new experimental details remain underspecified and Gemini iteration results are lost, but the diagnostic evidence resolves important gaps in v1 and supports a substantial net improvement.
